quests.instruction: Stretch the first sound in “moon” like a hum: mmm-oon. Which letter makes that sound?
quests.hint: Press your lips together and hum, then say moon. Does the hum come first?
quests.explanation: “Moon” starts with /m/, the humming sound that M writes. Your lips stay closed while it comes out.
quests.funFact: The /m/ sound travels out through your nose. Pinch your nose and try to hum it — it stops!

quests.instruction: A snake in the grass goes sssss. Which letter writes that hissing sound?
quests.hint: Smile a little and push air over your tongue. Can you make a long hiss?
quests.explanation: S writes the /s/ hiss you hear at the start of “snake”. You can stretch it out for as long as you have breath.

quests.instruction: Which letter makes the first sound in “tent”?
quests.hint: Tap the tip of your tongue just behind your top teeth. That quick tap is the sound you want.
quests.explanation: “Tent” begins with a quick /t/ tap, which is written with the letter T.

quests.instruction: Say “pear” with a little puff of air: p-p-pear. Which letter makes that first sound?
quests.hint: Hold your hand in front of your mouth. Can you feel the puff when your lips open?
quests.explanation: “Pear” starts with /p/. Your lips pop open and let out a puff of air. P is the letter for it.

quests.instruction: Which letter makes the /n/ sound, like the start of “net”?
quests.hint: Lift your tongue tip behind your top teeth and hum through your nose.
quests.explanation: N writes /n/. In “net” it is the very first sound, before the e and the t.

quests.instruction: Fork, fan and fun all begin with the same sound. Which letter writes it?
quests.hint: Rest your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow. What sound comes out?
quests.explanation: F writes the /f/ sound. Your top teeth touch your bottom lip while air flows out.
quests.funFact: Sometimes /f/ is written with two letters. In “phone” it is spelled ph — you will meet that later!

quests.instruction: Breathe on a cold window to fog it up: hhh. Which letter writes that breathy sound at the start of “hill”?
quests.hint: Pretend you are fogging up a mirror. The sound is only a gentle breath.
quests.explanation: The /h/ in “hill” is a soft puff of breath. H is the letter that writes it.

quests.instruction: Say “lamp” and listen for the very first sound. Which letter writes it?
quests.hint: Lift the tip of your tongue to the bumpy spot behind your top teeth: l-l-lamp.
quests.explanation: “Lamp” starts with /l/, made with your tongue tip up. L is the letter for it.

quests.instruction: Which letter makes the sound you hear at the start of “key”?
quests.hint: The sound comes from the back of your throat, a quick click: k-k-key.
quests.explanation: “Key” starts with /k/, which K writes. The letter C can make this sound too — you will see that soon.
quests.funFact: Many words that begin with /k/ before e or i use k, like key, kite and kitten.

quests.instruction: Pop your lips and add a little hum: b-b-bus. Which letter makes this sound?
quests.hint: Press your lips together, then let them pop open. Put a finger on your throat — can you feel a buzz?
quests.explanation: B writes /b/ at the start of “bus”. It is a lip pop with your voice switched on.
quests.funFact: The letters b and d look like mirror twins. Remember: b has its stick first and then its belly.

quests.instruction: Which letter starts the word “gift”? It makes the hard /g/ sound.
quests.hint: Say g-g-gift. Your throat does the work at the back of your mouth.
quests.explanation: “Gift” starts with the hard /g/ sound, written G. It is made at the back of the throat with your voice on.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with the /r/ sound?
quests.hint: Curl your tongue back a little and growl: rrr. Which word starts that way?
quests.explanation: “Rope” starts with /r/. “Sock” begins with /s/ and “tub” begins with /t/.

quests.instruction: Which letter spells the first sound of “duck”?
quests.hint: Tap your tongue behind your top teeth and add your voice: d-d-duck.
quests.explanation: “Duck” starts with /d/. D is the letter for it. Look at its shape: the round belly comes first, then the tall stick.
quests.funFact: The letter d is easy to remember as a drum and a drumstick: the round drum comes first.

quests.instruction: Round your lips like you are blowing a candle out, then say w-w-web. Which letter writes that sound?
quests.hint: Your lips make a small circle for this sound, and they do not touch your teeth.
quests.explanation: W writes /w/ at the start of “web”. Your lips are round, not closed.
quests.funFact: The name of the letter W is “double-u”, but its sound is just w-w-w.

quests.instruction: Jump, jam and jelly start with the same sound. Which letter writes it?
quests.hint: Your tongue presses up and then lets go with a buzz: j-j-jump.
quests.explanation: J writes /j/ at the start of “jump”, “jam” and “jelly”.

quests.instruction: Your top teeth touch your bottom lip and your voice hums. Which letter makes the first sound in “van”?
quests.hint: It is just like /f/, but with your voice turned on. Feel the buzz!
quests.explanation: V writes /v/, the buzzing partner of /f/. Both sounds are made the same way, but only /v/ uses your voice.
quests.funFact: Put a finger on your throat: /f/ is quiet, but /v/ buzzes.

quests.instruction: Which letter starts the words “yes” and “yellow”?
quests.hint: Smile and lift the middle of your tongue: y-y-yes. Which letter does that?
quests.explanation: At the start of a word, Y makes the /y/ sound, as in “yes” and “yellow”.
quests.funFact: Y is a busy letter. At the end of a word like “my” it works like a vowel.

quests.instruction: Which letter writes the first sound in “cap”? It sounds just like the first sound in “kite”.
quests.hint: Say cap, then say kite. Do the first sounds match? Pick the letter that spells cap.
quests.explanation: C can make the hard /k/ sound, as in “cap”, “cup” and “cat”.
quests.funFact: The letter C sometimes sounds like /k/ and sometimes like /s/. It works like two letters in one.

quests.instruction: Which of these words starts with /m/?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly. Only one starts with a hum and closed lips.
quests.explanation: “Mitten” begins with /m/. “Kitten” starts with /k/ and “button” with /b/.
quests.funFact: Changing just the first sound makes a whole new word: mitten, kitten, bitten.

quests.instruction: Z makes a buzzing sound, zzz, like a bee. Which word starts with /z/?
quests.hint: Put your fingers on your throat. One of these words starts with a buzz; another starts with a hiss.
quests.explanation: “Zipper” starts with the buzzing /z/. “Supper” starts with the hissing /s/, and “ladder” starts with /l/.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with the /w/ sound?
quests.hint: Round your lips first. Which word begins with that small circle?
quests.explanation: “Wagon” starts with /w/. “Valley” starts with /v/ and “yellow” with /y/.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with the same sound as “pan”?
quests.hint: Listen for the puff of air at the start of pan. Which word starts the same way?
quests.explanation: “Pan” and “pickle” both begin with /p/. “Bubble” begins with /b/, a close cousin that uses your voice.
quests.funFact: Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and say pan. It moves more for /p/ than it does for /b/.

quests.instruction: “Door” and one of these words begin with the same sound. Which word is it?
quests.hint: Tap your tongue behind your top teeth and switch your voice on.
quests.explanation: “Door” and “dinner” both start with /d/. “Tummy” starts with /t/ and “gate” with /g/.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT begin with /s/?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly. Two of them start with a hiss.
quests.explanation: “Sandal” and “soup” start with /s/. “Hammer” starts with the breathy /h/.

quests.instruction: Which small letter is the partner of the capital letter D?
quests.hint: Say “d” for “drum”: the round drum comes first, then the drumstick.
quests.explanation: Capital D and small d say the same /d/ sound. In small d, the belly is on the left and the stick is on the right.

quests.instruction: Which capital letter matches the small letter g?
quests.hint: Small g has a tail that drops below the line. Its capital is a big round shape with a little shelf.
quests.explanation: Capital G and small g both say /g/. They just look different.
quests.funFact: Names always start with a capital letter, like Gina.

quests.instruction: Which pair of letters, big and small, writes the /r/ at the start of “rain”?
quests.hint: Capital R looks like a P with a leg kicking out.
quests.explanation: R and r are the same letter in two sizes, and both say /r/.

quests.instruction: Say “lemon”, “lion” and “ladder”. Which letter do they all start with?
quests.hint: Lift your tongue tip up behind your top teeth each time.
quests.explanation: All three words begin with /l/, which L writes.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with the same sound as “kite”?
quests.hint: Feel the click at the back of your throat. Kite starts with a quick /k/.
quests.explanation: “Kite” and “kettle” both start with /k/. “Gate” starts with /g/, which uses your voice.
quests.funFact: K and hard C make the same sound, so kite and cake both start with /k/.

quests.instruction: Bus, bike and van are all things that roll. Which word starts with a different sound from the other two?
quests.hint: Compare bus and bike first. Do they start with the same lip pop?
quests.explanation: “Bus” and “bike” both start with /b/. “Van” starts with /v/, where your top teeth touch your lip.
